title: Choose the visual world for TPA Video Review
question: The roll assigned the Theater Program. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Theater Program
options.lineage: the printed program handed out at a TPA showcase night
options.thesis: Every video reads like the evening's program: a masthead, a scene listing, and a cast list where each anonymous participant has a line.
materials: program masthead band in TPA ink
options.viewport: Ink masthead with nav; under it the video title set like a program cover line, the player, then the timeline whose row labels are a cast list (Person_0001 ······ 0:00–2:28) and whose clip row is the scene listing; review panel at right.
options.risk: If the dot leaders and widths are set timidly it collapses into a plain admin table with a dark header.

raised.raise: Reject stands apart from Accept, Edit and Defer with deliberate space; panels divide by hairline rules, never shadows.
One text size does the body work; hierarchy comes from Archivo's weight and width axes, not a ladder of sizes.
Selecting a participant or clip lifts its timeline row and dims the rest, so the one in focus leads.
TPA orange has exactly one job: awaiting review. Nothing else on any screen is orange.
Every running time sits right-aligned in tabular figures, tight to its margin, like a program's scene timings.
Times, counts and scores print in full ink, never as faded gray.

options.label: Ensemble Score
options.lineage: a band or choir arrangement with one staff per performer
options.thesis: The timeline is an ensemble score: one staff per participant, boxed rehearsal letters for review clips, bar numbers for time.
options.viewport: Top nav; the player; beneath it a score system with participant staves, rehearsal-letter clip markers (A, B, C…) and annotations sitting on their staff.
options.risk: The most literal arts metaphor of my list; dance, theater and visual-art staff may read music notation as someone else's world.

options.label: Dark Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels split by hairline seams with syntax-colored state.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dark monitoring console over footage of teens reads as surveillance.
options.risk: Cold and clinical for this audience.
options.kept: Reject isolated by deliberate space; hairlines instead of shadows.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Section-hued divider boards under clear acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the fore edge.
options.case: Fuses poorly: staff have no tie to software manuals and the tab rail fights standard navigation.
options.kept: One text size does the work.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of poster tiles; the focused one grows and the rest dim.
options.viewport: Horizontally scrolling rows of video tiles.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it needs footage thumbnails as its only color and hides metadata until focus.
options.risk: Entertainment framing for a review job.
options.kept: The row in focus leads and the rest dim.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.thesis: Yellow bands that mean one thing: the way to go.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no audience tie, and monumental signage is loud for long sessions.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Timed tracklists in ballpoint on lined inlay stock.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hand lettering undercuts staff authority on a working screen.
options.kept: Running times right-aligned, tabular, tight to the margin.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields and sine lattices.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cold, machine-first, and the opposite of humans-decide.
options.kept: Numbers in full ink, never gray.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light review tool in the vein of modern video-review SaaS, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left sidebar, player, timeline, inspector panel.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any SaaS dashboard, the look you asked to avoid.
